quotes.text: If you set a custom cancel date, you can’t provide a refund. You can also only prevent the credit proration from generating if the `cancel_at` date is within the current billing period. If you cancel the subscription for a date outside the current period, you can’t disable the proration.
To prevent billing your customer for pending invoice items, you must [manually delete](https://docs.stripe.com/api.md#delete_invoiceitem) the invoice items.
The workflow runs when the subscription ends and deletes only its pending invoice items.

When `cancel_at` shortens the current billing period, [disabling prorations](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/prorations.md#disable-prorations) can have different invoice line effects depending on the subscription’s [billing mode](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/billing-mode.md).

old_evidence.text: If you set a custom cancellation date, you can’t provide a refund. A credit proration is always generated. To prevent a credit proration from generating, make sure the custom cancellation date is within the current billing period and `proration_behavior` is set to `none`.
When you cancel a subscription, all `open` and `draft` invoices for that subscription have their `auto_advance` property set to `false`.

findings: The same captured URL still documents immediate, period-end, schedule, dispute-triggered and custom-date cancellation (new 17-88, 141-176; old 16-94, 147-184). Immediate cancellation is the default for a manual cancel call, stops future subscription invoices and leaves only metadata and cancellation_details updateable (new 19; old 18). A scheduled period-end cancellation can be stopped before the period ends; a canceled subscription cannot be reactivated (new 64, 118-139; old 70, 120-145).

Current source 42 and concept custom-date section say a credit proration is always generated. Old raw 20 itself provided a within-period suppression path, and new 21 states only that prevention is possible when cancel_at is within the current billing period. New 151-153 says shortening the current period creates prorations unless disabled, with billing-mode-dependent invoice-line effects. New 166 explicitly rules out disabling prorations for a cancel date beyond the current period. Do not infer that being within the current period alone suppresses a proration, or that suppression has identical invoice consequences in every billing mode.

The new page adds a Workflows template that runs when the subscription ends and deletes only pending invoice items for that subscription (new 105-107). This is an optional no-code automation route; it does not retroactively delete items, erase invoices, or change the separate existing manual-delete guidance at new 92-103 and old 98-109. A final invoice or another active subscription can still bill pending items absent deletion.

The unchanged invoice boundary is material: cancellation sets auto_advance=false on open and draft invoices for that subscription, pausing automatic collection and reminders, while manual collection and emails remain possible (new 103; old 109). It does not mean those invoices are voided or debts discharged. If cancel_at_period_end is set, pending prorations remain for period end; an early cancel leaves invoice items unprocessed unless specifically invoiced (new 101; old 107).

Event identity remains unchanged: customer.subscription.updated includes scheduling cancel_at_period_end, whereas customer.subscription.deleted marks actual cancellation by direct deletion or period-end arrival (new 109-116; old 111-118). Do not treat the scheduling update as the deletion or a paid final invoice.

The new and old pages both restrict dispute-triggered cancellation to full-amount credit or debit card disputes, exclude test clocks, say changes take roughly an hour, and release scheduled subscriptions before cancellation (new 74-88; old 80-94). Neither capture establishes that any merchant configured this setting or that any specific dispute canceled a subscription.

The older Node.js examples become curl examples in the new capture (old 35-41, 60-68, 135-159; new 36-39, 58-62, 133-149). This is a rendering change, not a new required SDK or a demonstrated API execution. The prior 2018-02-28 update-parameter warning and post-June-2024 anchor guarantee persist (old 145, 182; new 139, 174).
substantive_changes: New wording clarifies custom-date proration boundaries: within-period is a necessary condition for preventing the credit proration; outside-current-period cancel_at cannot disable prorations, and billing mode can change invoice-line effects when the period is shortened (new 21, 151-166 versus old 20, 161-174).
New optional Workflows template deletes only pending invoice items after the subscription ends (new 105-107); existing manual-deletion and invoice-collection rules remain (new 90-103; old 96-109).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the old 2026-05-13 capture's custom-date statement dated, including its explicit proration_behavior=none within-period suppression path (old 20), rather than repeating its internally overbroad 'always generated' sentence as a universal rule.

Preserve unchanged irreversible canceled status, period-end reactivation cutoff, invoice-item and auto_advance effects, event distinction, full-amount-card-dispute limitation, 2018-02-28 warning, and post-June-2024 anchor qualification (old 18, 70, 84-109, 117-145, 182; new 19, 64, 78-103, 115-139, 174).
Keep old Node.js examples as dated sample code, not a current compulsory SDK path (old 35-41, 60-68; new 36-39, 58-62).
conflicts: Current source 42 and wiki/concepts/stripe-subscriptions-cancel.md custom-date section assert an always-generated credit proration while both old 20 and new 21 allow a bounded within-period prevention path. New 153 adds billing-mode-dependent line effects.

Current source 62 and concept invoice-items section say pending invoice items 'must manually delete' without noting the new optional Workflows route. The no-code template operates only when the subscription ends and only on its pending items (new 105-107), so the manual instruction remains valid when the workflow is not used.
unresolved_questions: The capture does not determine the exact invoice line effects for each billing mode when prorations are disabled; new 153 links to a separate comparison guide, which was not used as behavioral evidence here.
The page does not establish that the Workflows template is installed or run for any particular account, nor prove the deletion timing and result of a specific invoice item.
The capture does not prove a refund, payment collection, final invoice settlement, or any merchant's automatic-cancellation configuration.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/cancel, the new capture documents immediate cancellation by API or Dashboard, pending period-end cancellation, custom future dates, schedules and limited dispute-triggered cancellation (new 17-88, 141-176). A canceled subscription cannot be reactivated; a period-end cancellation can be stopped before the period ends (new 64, 118-131; old 70, 120-133). Cancellation stops future subscription invoices, while open and draft invoices have auto_advance disabled rather than being erased (new 19, 103; old 18, 109). [[source-stripe-subscriptions-cancel]] covers these routes but overstates custom-date credit proration at source 42. The new page adds a scoped Workflows option for deleting pending invoice items when the subscription ends (new 105-107).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/cancel, the main substantive changes are clearer custom-date proration limits and a no-code pending-item deletion template (new 21, 105-107, 151-166; old 20, 96-109, 161-174). [[source-stripe-subscriptions-cancel]] and its concept should replace the universal 'credit proration always generated' claim: within-period dates permit suppression, while a date outside the current period cannot disable proration, and billing mode can alter invoice-line effects. The prior proration_behavior=none guidance remains dated at old 20. Node.js-to-curl examples, list numbering, link phrasing and emphasis are presentational. Distinguish customer.subscription.updated for scheduling from customer.subscription.deleted for actual cancellation (new 115-116; old 117-118), and do not infer any refund, invoice payment, workflow execution, or account eligibility from this capture.
